chunks: My father (Al-Husayn ibn Idris), from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, from his forefathers, (peace be upon them), said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Charity prevents an unpleasant death.'

key_terms.مِيتَةَ السَّوْءِ: Unpleasant death (death from calamity or in a state of sin)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of giving Sadaqah regarding one's death?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) conveys the Prophet’s (s.a.w.) promise that charity acts as a shield against *Mitat al-Saw'* (an unpleasant death), a concept Shia scholars interpret as protection from the pangs of death, sudden calamity, or dying in a state of sin. This narration underscores the eschatological efficacy of *Sadaqah* not merely as social welfare, but as a spiritual safeguard ensuring a dignified transition to the afterlife.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 8.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his predecessors that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “
Sadaqah keeps one away from unpleasant death.”
